thread.title: Visa (V) shares present a clear long-term uptrend

author: Mary Chesterton
title: Visa (V) shares present a clear long-term uptrend
text:
Visa (V) shares present a clear long-term uptrend March 23, 2018 tweet 
Visa (V) shares gained more than 37% in the last year, driven by the solid financial performance of the business. At current price levels, its valuation is demanding, although the credit card company has proven to have extraordinary quality and exceptional levels of profitability. 
A quality asset 
Visa is the undisputed market leader in the electronic payments industry. The company has a market share of more than 50% in credit cards worldwide, and its degree of participation in debit cards is even higher. To the extent that consumers around the world are replacing paper money with more efficient alternatives, the firm is in a privileged position to capitalize on that trend. 
Visa has one of the most recognized brands in the market, and its payment network includes 16,800 financial institutions, 44 million merchants and billions of cards in the hands of users around the world. The scale of the business is a key differential factor and a strategic strategic advantage for the firm. 
In recent years, major technology players such as Apple (AAPL) and Google (GOOG) (GOOGL) have entered the digital payments market, while smaller players, such as PayPal (PYPL), are rapidly expanding their presence in that business. . 
Fortunately for investors in Visa, these companies have decided to ally with the market leader instead of competing too aggressively. Clearly, the competitive strategy of technology companies has to do with the strengths of Visa, both in terms of its brand power and the scale of the business. 
Their numbers show that the business is in very good health. Visa sales in the last quarter amounted to 4,860 million dollars, an increase of 9% compared to the same quarter of the previous year. The figure surpassed the forecasts of the analysts in 20 million dollars. 
In the same sense, adjusted earnings per share were $ 1.08, up 26% year-on-year. Wall Street analysts expected a lower value, in the area of ​​0.99 per unit on average. 
The profitability levels of the business are truly extraordinary: Visa’s operating profit margin is in the area of ​​68% over billing. In terms of return on capital, the company generates a return on equity of 26%. 
Visa shares quote at a plausible valuation. The price-earnings ratio is in the area of ​​27.4 times the expected earnings for the company in the next year. Depending on the quality of the asset, it is possible to justify a valuation above the market average, although it should not be forgotten that the entry price represents a risk in case the business performance does not match the expectations in the medium term. 
Regulatory risk is another key variable to consider. Since Visa occupies a dominant position in a highly profitable market, governments in different countries usually set limits on the fees that the firm can charge, which obviously impacts its profit margins. 
In the industry, some major technological changes are also taking place. The boom in digital payments has driven big players in the technology market to jump into payment processing. In the same sense, Blockchain technologies present a clearly disruptive potential in this business segment. 
Visa has formidable competitive advantages thanks to the size of its network and the value of the brand. These strengths should be valuable when it comes to protecting your business. In addition, the trend seems to be that the main players in the market seek to associate and create alliances instead of competing aggressively. Beyond this, it is important to monitor the ecosystem of the payments industry and Visa’s ability to maintain its leadership position in it. 
Technically, the shares of the card company present a clear long-term uptrend. The recent adjustment of prices generated a transitory break of this tendency, although the values ​​managed to recover and resume the upward trend above the area of ​​120 dollars per share. This level is important in the short term, since it indicates the continuity or not of the upward price trend. 
A break below the trend line could lead the asset to test again the area of ​​115-110 dollars per unit. This level worked as support during the adjustment observed in the month of February. On the contrary, in case it manages to sustain the upward trend in prices, a new test of the historical price maximums for Visa is likely, in the area of ​​127 dollars per share. 
On average, Wall Street analysts have a target price of $140.23 for Visa shares. This value represents a bullish potential of around 16% compared to current levels. TAGS
